correctness.rationale: The absolute-Gaussian representation is exactly hemisphere-uniform. The Gaussian quadratic-form characteristic function has an identity covariance and only triangular nonzero third joint cumulants among distinct edges. Fourier inversion gives an integrated error \(O_k(d^{-1})\) first-order density expansion, and signed orthant integration yields identical \((2/\pi)^{3/2}\) coefficients for edges and triangles. The H shift has finite moments; normalization and sign cases agree with independent finite diagnostics. The analysis is fixed \(k\), sufficiently large d; finite checks do not establish the universal statement.

value.rationale: A fixed set of random hemisphere directions induces a natural acute-angle graph. The result determines all of its induced signed graph probabilities at first non-Gaussian order, showing that exactly two structural motifs (edges and triangles) govern the correction. It distinguishes boundary-induced individual-edge bias from intrinsic triangle dependence and yields a closed sharp asymptotic for pairwise-acute k-configurations. This is a complete motivated joint law, not a parameter-substituted scalar angle calculation.
